# Omnispherepop

> Weight programming for humans and agents: ternary quantization, ultra-graphs,
> reversible weight diffs, and an academy that teaches by making you move real
> weights. Rust core, thin adapters, zero accounts, zero telemetry.

Omnispherepop is a mutual product of Peter Lodri Sec, 88B (8b-is), and Standard
Galactic. Licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0.

## What this file is

`llms.txt` is a compact map for language models and coding agents: what the project
is, where the truth lives, and what the current capabilities actually are. It is
generated from the same facts as the README, and `docs/STATUS.md` is the authority
when they disagree.

## Start here

- [README.md](https://github.com/omnispherepop/omnispherepop/blob/main/README.md): 30-second tour, install, agent usage
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/omnispherepop/omnispherepop/blob/main/AGENTS.md): rules for coding agents working in this repo
- [docs/STATUS.md](https://github.com/omnispherepop/omnispherepop/blob/main/docs/STATUS.md): what is verified, what is not
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/omnispherepop/omnispherepop/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): invariants, module seams, why one operation set
- [docs/ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/omnispherepop/omnispherepop/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md): what comes next, in dependency order
- [docs/CURRICULUM.md](https://github.com/omnispherepop/omnispherepop/blob/main/docs/CURRICULUM.md): all 17 lessons with prerequisites and checkpoints

## Capabilities (current)

- Ternary quantization to `{-1, 0, +1}` with per-group scales; reports sparsity,
  packed bytes, and RMSE computed from the data.
- Two calibrations: `ternary` (Δ = 0.7·mean|w| per group) and `qdelta` (the
  ultra-graph A6P Q16.16 rule, from the `zerocpu` submodule).
- Two ternary packings: 4 trits per byte (core) and 5 trits per byte (ultra-graph).
- Immutable content-addressed snapshots with reversible diffs.
- Ultra-graphs with set-to-set edges and fixed-point reachability.
- safetensors reading for dense F32/F16/BF16 tensors, with strict rejection of
  unsupported dtypes, overlapping ranges, and non-finite payloads.
- A committed real checkpoint, `examples/tiny-gpt2.safetensors`, used by tests.
- MCP server over stdio with nine tools; ACP, desktop, and WASM are not built.
- A static site with a browser reference kernel that is parity-checked against Rust.

## Not available

No desktop app, no Python package on PyPI, no WASM build, no native installers, no
ACP endpoint, no GGUF reader, no trained model, and no published quality benchmark.
`docs/STATUS.md` records these as open rather than done.

## Machine-readable entry points

- MCP: run `ospop-mcp` and speak JSON-RPC over stdio. `tools/list` returns nine
  tools: `ospop_load_demo`, `ospop_load_safetensors`, `ospop_inspect`,
  `ospop_quantize`, `ospop_lens`, `ospop_prune`, `ospop_diff`, `ospop_explain`,
  `ospop_learn`.
- CLI: every command has a `--json` form; parse it instead of the text output.
  `ospop learn --json` returns the whole curriculum with checkpoints.
- Agent plugin: `agent-plugin/` contains a plugin manifest, MCP wiring, and skills
  for harnesses that support them.
